title: Quantum materials QED with van der Waals crystals
authors: Suheng Xu, Brian Vermilyea, Ran Jing, Lukas Wehmeier, Jihoon Park, Rafael A. Mayer, Xinzhong Chen, Samuel L. Moore, Fuyang Tay, Boyi Zhou, Wenjun Zheng, Dihao Sun, Birui Yang, Cory R. Dean, Daniel Cazorla, Xu Du, Milan Delor, Andrew J. Millis, Angel Rubio, Michael M. Fogler, Mengkun Liu, D. N. Basov
abstract: A central goal of the emerging field of materials QED is to harness subwavelength electromagnetic confinement in engineered cavities to tailor light-matter interactions. Here, we demonstrate that van der Waals multilayer cavities composed of stacked graphene and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) provide unprecedented control over hybridization between their electromagnetic resonances. By magnetically tuning graphene inter-Landau-level transitions (ILTs) into resonance with hBN phonons, we witness broadband, mode-selective strong coupling in the mid-infrared. Our quantum-material QED framework shows that cavity geometry and layer placement jointly control both coupling strength and modal selectivity. For experimentally realistic cavity parameters, the predicted mode splitting exceeds the width of the hBN Reststrahlen band, providing a direct route to the ultrastrong coupling regime. Together, these results establish van der Waals multilayer cavities as a scalable platform for tunable multimode QED and broaden the design space for reconfigurable quantum materials.
summary: This paper proposes using van der Waals multilayer cavities of graphene and hBN to engineer strong light-matter interactions for quantum electrodynamics. By magnetically tuning graphene's electronic transitions into resonance with hBN phonons, the authors predict broadband, mode-selective coupling. This establishes the multilayer structure as a highly tunable and scalable platform for realizing ultrastrong coupling regimes.
main_problem: The central goal is to develop a scalable platform for tunable multimode Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) by engineering light-matter interactions using subwavelength confinement.
main_result: The study demonstrates that van der Waals multilayer cavities composed of graphene and hBN can achieve broadband, mode-selective strong coupling, potentially reaching the ultrastrong coupling regime.
method: The authors developed a quantum material QED framework involving the quantization of confined electromagnetic fields and deriving the system Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The physical system is a van der Waals multilayer cavity made of stacked graphene and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The model incorporates magnetically tunable Inter-Landau-Level Transitions (ILTs) in graphene coupled to hyperbolic phonon resonances in hBN.
key_observables: Mode splitting ($\Delta$), coupling strength, and mode hybridization between ILTs and phonons.
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength (tuning ILTs), cavity geometry (layer placement, number of layers $N$), and the ratio $\Delta/\omega_0$ (for ultrastrong coupling).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a spatially local continuum model for hBN and neglects direct electrostatic coupling between different graphene layers.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the multilayer cavity, showing mode hybridization via avoided crossings in the dispersion relation, and comparing uncoupled versus coupled mode dispersions.
paper_structure: The paper builds the QED Hamiltonian by incorporating graphene ILTs and hBN phonon modes, analyzes the resulting mode hybridization, and establishes the multilayer structure as a tunable platform for strong coupling.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses cavity QED in solid-state systems, providing a detailed theoretical roadmap for engineering strong light-matter coupling using tunable quantum materials, which is highly relevant to AMO physics.

Spintronics.note: The paper's core mechanism involves coupling electronic transitions (ILTs in graphene) to optical/phonon modes within a structured material (van der Waals cavity), directly addressing the interface between quantum optics and magnetic/electronic systems relevant to cavity QED in spintronics.
